Frequently Asked Questions

Do heat pumps actually hold up in foothills cold, or should Marietta homes stick with gas?

Modern cold-climate heat pumps hold useful capacity well below freezing, which covers typical foothills winters. Homes that want gas security can pair both in a dual fuel setup that switches automatically at the economic crossover. The load calculation and your fuel access decide the configuration.

How often should a standby generator be serviced if it rarely runs?

Annually at minimum, plus its own self-test cycle weekly. Standby engines fail from sitting, not from running: stale fuel issues, weak batteries, and seized components all develop in idle equipment. Annual service catches them while they are maintenance items instead of discoveries mid-outage.

My water leaves rust stains and tastes metallic. What is the fix?

Start with a water test, because the treatment has to match the measurement. Staining and metallic taste typically trace to iron or manganese levels that specific filtration handles well. Guessing at equipment wastes money; testing takes one visit and makes the correction specific.

Where should carbon monoxide detectors go in a home with a wood stove and gas furnace?

On every level of the home and outside sleeping areas, with placement following each detector’s mounting requirements. Homes running multiple combustion sources should also have the equipment itself checked seasonally, since detection is the backstop and sound venting is the actual protection.
